correctness.rationale: Substituting p1=p2=p3=p and n=2p into the source coloring equations forces one common parity. Taniguchi's affine-endomorphism lemma then makes the projective class of the two normalized difference coordinates invariant under every nonconstant image. There are p+1 projective classes, each of size 2p(p-1), with exactly two affine maps between any ordered pair inside a class and exactly two maps from any nontrivial coloring to any fixed constant coloring. Theorem 29 instead merges p-2 of these classes into one complete block, a decisive discrepancy already at p=5.

value.rationale: The finding refutes a central structural theorem of a fresh knot-theory preprint on an infinite family, not merely a numerical example. It identifies the exact mechanism of failure: a claimed giant complete block splits into p-2 projectively separated components. The smallest witness is explicit and the all-prime repair supplies a reusable boundary condition for any corrected composite-modulus theorem.
